title: Intermediate MEC / CEC (Regular)
tagline: Build a strong academic foundation in Mathematics, Economics, Commerce, and Civics with a structured Intermediate programme designed to prepare students for higher education and diverse career opportunities.
overview:
This programme is designed for students pursuing Intermediate MEC/CEC who want to develop a strong foundation in commerce, economics, mathematics, and related subjects. The curriculum focuses on conceptual understanding, academic excellence, and essential skills needed for higher education.
Through structured classroom learning, regular assessments, and academic guidance, students are prepared for a wide range of future pathways in Commerce, Management, Economics, Finance, Law, and other professional fields.
highlights: Choice of MEC or CEC stream
Strong foundation in Economics and Commerce
Career guidance for higher education and professional courses
eligibility: Pass in Class 10 (SSC / CBSE / ICSE or equivalent).
board: Board of Intermediate Education, Andhra Pradesh

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Pass in Class 10 (SSC / CBSE / ICSE or equivalent)

sections.heading: MEC / CEC Course Structure & Examination Pattern
paragraphs: The Intermediate course under BIE-AP has two public examinations — at the end of First Year and Second Year — and is structured as:

items.text: Part II: Second Language (Sanskrit / Telugu / Hindi)
Part III: Group subjects, each with two papers (one per year)

closing_paragraphs: MEC: Mathematics (IA & IB in First Year; IIA & IIB in Second Year), Economics, Commerce

MEC is the recommended group for students targeting CA, CMA, CS, IPM/BBA at IIMs, B.Com. (Hons.), Economics (Hons.), actuarial science, statistics and data-driven careers. CEC suits students who prefer a non-mathematical route into commerce, law, civil services, public administration, journalism and management.

sections.heading: Specializations
paragraphs: MEC / CEC. Integrated add-ons: CA/CMA Foundation, IPMAT, CLAT. CA Foundation track / CMA Foundation track (students choose one; the Intermediate MEC syllabus is common to both). CLAT/AILET focus; AP LAWCET focus; Law + Commerce (B.B.A. LL.B. / B.Com. LL.B. orientation).
